Markdown can be used in the GitHub web interface. In this article About creating diagrams You can create diagrams in Markdown using four different syntaxes: mermaid, geoJSON, topoJSON, and ASCII STL. Diagram rendering is available in GitHub Issues, GitHub Discussions, pull requests, wikis, and Markdown files. Creating Mermaid diagrams Mermaid is a Markdown-inspired tool that renders text into diagrams. For example, Mermaid can render flow charts, sequence diagrams, pie charts and more. For more information, see the Mermaid documentation . To create a Mermaid diagram, add Mermaid syntax inside a fenced code block with the mermaid language identifier. For more information about creating code blocks, see Creating and highlighting code blocks . For example, you can create a flow chart by specifying values and arrows. Here is a simple flow chart: ```mermaid graph TD; A-->B; A-->C; B-->D; C-->D; ``` Note You may observe errors if you run a third-party Mermaid plugin when using Mermaid syntax on GitHub. Checking your version of Mermaid To ensure GitHub supports your Mermaid syntax, check the Mermaid version currently in use. ```mermaid info ``` Creating GeoJSON and TopoJSON maps You can use GeoJSON or TopoJSON syntax to create interactive maps. pages.text: Creating gists - GitHub Docs Skip to main content Skip to content Collapse sidebar Expand sidebar In this article Creating gists You can create two kinds of gists: public and secret. Create a public gist if you're ready to share your ideas with the world or a secret gist if you're not. Copy markdown In this article About gists Gists provide a simple way to share code snippets with others. Every gist is a Git repository, which means that it can be forked and cloned. If you are signed in to GitHub when you create a gist, the gist will be associated with your account and you will see it in your list of gists when you navigate to your gist home page . Gists can be public or secret. Public gists show up in Discover , where people can browse new gists as they're created. They're also searchable, so you can use them if you'd like other people to find and see your work. Secret gists don't show up in Discover and are not searchable unless you are logged in and are the author of the secret gist. Secret gists aren't private. If you send the URL of a secret gist to a friend, they'll be able to see it. However, if someone you don't know discovers the URL, they'll also be able to see your gist. If you need to keep your code away from prying eyes, you may want to create a private repository instead. For GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub automatically scans secret gists for partner secrets and informs the relevant partner whenever one of their secrets is leaked. pages.text: Creative Ground Schools Workshop | Tate Britain Explore the connections between plants, gardens and art through hands-on gardening, creative making and close observation Transforming how young people connect with plants, growing, art and the important questions shaping our world today. Creative Ground is a new, free, pre-booked experience for all schools, created in partnership between the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) and Tate Britain. Set across the Clore Garden Classroom, Clore Garden and Tate Britain gallery spaces, Creative Ground invites young people to discover the connections between horticulture, nature and creativity. Creative Ground is a partnership between the RHS and Tate Britain, generously supported by the Clore Duffield Foundation. About the workshop Every learner will take part in practical gardening activities that encourage learners to investigate the living world first-hand, developing skills and confidence. Through creative making, discussion and reflection, learners will consider how they observe, connect and draw inspiration from the natural world. Learners will explore the joy, inspiration and sense of connection that gardens and art can foster. By bringing together horticulture and art, Creative Ground encourages young people to see themselves as active participants in shaping a more positive future. As part of the experience, schools will take part in a connected programme of learning that combines a facilitated session in the Clore Garden Classroom with resources designed to link learning across the garden, gallery and classroom. pages.description: The 2018 scandal has resurfaced this month after Usman Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about the cheating plot.
pages.text: Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Cricket Australia hopes the 'forum' will help the sport move on By Simon Atkinson and Tiffanie Turnbull Sydney Published 18 November 2026, 03:52 GMT Updated 1 hour ago Cricket Australia has launched an independent "forum" for players and staff involved in the sandpapergate scandal to share their version of events. In a memoir released earlier this month, former player Usman Khawaja claimed the entire Australia team knew of the plot to tamper with the ball during a 2018 Test in South Africa, contradicting the investigation at the time. His comments have led to a bitter split among former and current players and have overshadowed the beginning of Australia's international cricket season. The forum was not a new investigation and there will be no new penalties, Cricket Australia said, adding that nobody would be forced to take part. However, chief executive Todd Greenberg said he hoped the discussions would allow the sport to "move on". "The game is genuinely hurting at the moment. It's not good for anyone," he said. "We need to find a path through and we need some time to heal." The sandpapergate scandal is often described as one of Australian cricket's darkest days and was a source of national shame. pages.description: Scotland beat United Arab Emirates by one wicket as Jasper Davidson struck the winning boundary with just one ball to spare in a dramatic finish to their Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 Tri-Series match in Dundee.
pages.text: Cricket World Cup League 2 Tri-Series: Scotland scrape one-wicket win over UAE on penultimate ball - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jasper Davidson struck the winning runs Published 9 August 2026 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 Tri-Series United Arab Emirates 231-8 (40 overs): Usmani 116 (126); McMullen 3-30 Scotland 235-9 (39.5): Cross 66 (51), Jones 44 (52); Jawadullah 3-47 Scotland won by one wicket Scoreboard Scotland beat United Arab Emirates by one wicket as Jasper Davidson struck the winning boundary with just one ball to spare in a dramatic finish to their Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 Tri-Series match in Dundee. It came two days after a nine-run win over Canada at the same Forthill venue sealed their place at next year's World Cup Qualifier. This time the hosts were set a target of 231, with wicketkeeper and opener Adeeb Usmani scoring an impressive 116, including three sixes and 11 fours, after the visitors were put into bat and made their total for the loss of eight wickets. With experienced batsmen George Munsey and Brandon McMullen - the pick of the bowlers earlier with 3-30 - falling for ducks, the Scots looked in trouble at 2-2. But Finlay McCreath (28) and Richie Berrington (39) steadied the ship and while Michael Jones (44) and Matthew Cross (66) put on 72 for the fifth wicket, it could not prevent a grandstand finish. It was down to Davidson to hit the winning boundary off the penultimate ball after running two to level the scores off the previous delivery, with his match-winning shot leaving Scotland on 235-9. pages.text: Criminal Division | Beware of Scammers Skip to main content Beware of Scammers Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email Criminals are impersonating Criminal Division personnel to commit fraud. These criminals may contact victims by phone, email, SMS (text message), encrypted applications, social media, or a letter from someone pretending to be from the U.S. Department of Justice’s Criminal Division. Although their approaches may vary, these actors are typically seeking to secure your private information including personally identifiable information (PII) or bank account information, or to convince you an urgent matter requires you to release money to resolve the issue. Criminal Division personnel will not contact members of the public via SMS (text message), Telegram, Signal, WhatsApp, or similar encrypted mobile applications to solicit money via wire, online transfer, or crypto currency, or to threaten to freeze bank accounts. If you suspect a scam, stop communicating immediately. Do not transfer funds to anyone claiming to act on behalf of or to represent the Criminal Division or any of its sections . He said he was deployed to Iraq, and was looking for love after he had lost his wife in a car crash about two years prior. His 5-year-old boy was staying with his sister while he was deployed, he told her. Shelly was enthralled but, as a single mom, remained cautious. While not a humanitarian organization , the ILO plays a vital role in prevention, recovery and reconstruction, by assessing the impacts of crises on jobs and businesses, strengthening social protection systems, and supporting workers’ and employers’ organizations in crisis response. Today, around 2 billion people live in fragile and conflict-affected settings , and more than 117 million are forcibly displaced, most exposed to severe disaster risks. Women and girls are disproportionately affected, with 612 million now living in conflict zones. These crises disrupt livelihoods, weaken institutions and labour markets, and deepen decent work deficits. They also intensify inequalities, often worsening women’s working conditions while increasing unpaid care responsibilities, with long-term risks for poverty, stability and social cohesion. pages.description: Interstate Air Pollution Transport, also known as Air Transport, is when air pollution travels over distances, affecting air quality and public health locally and regionally.

Cross-State Air Pollution The total pollution in any area forms from the combination of local and upwind sources. Air transport refers to pollution from upwind emission sources that impact air quality in a given location downwind. Emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) and nitrogen oxides (NO X ) can each undergo chemical reactions in the atmosphere to form fine particle (soot) pollution. Similarly, NO X emissions can react in the atmosphere to create ground-level ozone (smog) pollution. These pollutants can travel great distances affecting air quality and public health regionally. The transport of these pollutants across state borders, referred to as interstate air pollution transport, makes it difficult for downwind states to meet health-based air quality standards for PM 2.5 and ozone. The "Good Neighbor" Provision The Clean Air Act 's "good neighbor" provision requires EPA and states to address interstate transport of air pollution that affects downwind states' ability to attain and maintain National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) . pages.title: Crossmark button guidelines - Crossref
pages.description:
It’s important that all members use the Crossmark button consistently, to make sure it is familiar to readers and can be easily recognised.
The Crossmark button is available in color and monochrome versions, and can be resized to suit your website or PDFs. It must not otherwise be altered or adapted. We recommend using the color button on HTML pages, and either the color or monochrome button on PDFs for maximum user recognition.

This module is no longer part of the Python standard library. It was removed in Python 3.13 after being deprecated in Python 3.11. The removal was decided in PEP 594 . Applications can use the hashlib module from the standard library. Other possible replacements are third-party libraries from PyPI: legacycrypt , bcrypt , or argon2-cffi . These are not supported or maintained by the Python core team. The last version of Python that provided the crypt module was Python 3.12 . Cryptography uses mathematical techniques to protect the security of information. As our electronic networks grow increasingly open and interconnected, it is crucial to have strong, trusted cryptographic standards and guidelines, algorithms and encryption methods that can be used for e-commerce transactions, mobile device conversations and other exchanges of data. pages.text: Crystal Palace news: Tottenham's Van de Ven lucky to escape injury from Mateta challenge - FA commission - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images By Dale Johnson Football issues correspondent Published 11 November 2026 Micky van de Ven was "fortunate not to have suffered a debilitating injury" from a challenge by Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta, a Football Association regulatory commission has said. Mateta was sent off for the foul, which came in the 13th minute of the Eagles' 2-0 defeat by Tottenham Hotspur on 31 October. The France international was initially shown a yellow card by referee Michael Oliver, which was upgraded to red after a video assistant referee (VAR) review. Palace's appeal was turned down by the regulatory commission last week, with the written reasons now published. The verdict of the three members of commission was unanimous, with strong feelings about the nature of the foul. In their evidence, Palace argued that "their player's challenge was controlled, directed solely at winning the ball, and did not involve excessive force, brutality, or any action that endangered the safety of his opponent". The South London club also believed that Van de Ven's movement was a contributory factor, and the VAR review was unnecessary because Oliver had "the best evidence of the true speed and intensity of the challenge". In reaching its judgement, the commission said that Mateta "reached for the ball with a lunging action along the ground with a straight leg and his studs showing" which caught the Netherlands international "with gathering momentum".
